items.title: Jensen Huang: Why a personal scandal for the face of the AI boom has provoked a national security scare
items.summary: Jensen Huang is one of the technology industry's most high-profile figures He rose to prominence as the business he leads - artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia - became one of the world's most valuable companies As the face of the AI boom, Huang also became close to Donald Trump as the president pushed for the US to keep its dominance of the technology over China The 63-year-old who was once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" and referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan is now mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia He has an estimated fortune of $155bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine - a biography on Huang, tells the BBC…

items.title: Italy announces 2027 business mission to Mozambique, with tourism at its heart
items.summary: The delegation also included the President of the Mozambique–Italy Chamber of Commerce, Simone Santi, and the Deputy Head of the Maputo office of the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation, Cristina Pescante, as well as representatives of several Italian companies operating in the country Speaking during the panel dedicated to Italian investment, Ambassador Annis announced that the Italian business mission planned for 2027 would focus specifically on tourism, with the aim of showcasing Mozambique’s vast potential and numerous opportunities to Italian investors, as well as helping to increase tourist flows to and from Italy The summit was opened by President Daniel Chapo, who reaffirmed tourism as a key sector for the Mozambique’s development and announced several measures to boost the sector, including opening up the aviation market, integration into regional circuits, simplification of administrative procedures and an active visa policy Source: Embaixada da Itália em Maputo / Ambasciata d’Italia a Maputo

items.title: Police kills three for alleged attempt to rob a residence
items.summary: Maputo, 09 Nov (AIM) – On Monday morning, three individuals were shot dead by Mozambican Police (PRM), in Infulene neighborhood, southern municipality of Matola, for allegedly attempting to rob a residence that also serves as a facility of microcredit establishment. According to the PRM spokesperson, the victims were shot dead during an exchange of gunfire with the Police. The spokesperson explained that police officers were on patrol when they noticed suspicious individuals in the vicinity of the residence. As the officers approached to investigate, the suspects opened fire, and the Police retaliated, resulting in the deaths of three of the four group members. Preliminary information, provided by the Police, the individuals intended to break into the property to steal funds belonging to the owner, a man of Asian descent who operates a microcredit business and who had previously been targeted by criminals. The police confirmed that two of the suspects were armed, and two firearms have been recovered.

items.title: Over 4,000 road accidents recorded over last four years
items.summary: Maputo, 09 Nov (AIM) – Mozambique’s National Statistics Institute (INE) recorded over the last four years the death of 4,318 lives as a result of road accidents that took place throughout the country. According to INE annual report – which covers the period between 2021 and 2025 – since 2021, when 1,027 road accidents were recorded, the number of crashes has fallen by 40.5 percent, representing 416 fewer incidents over four years. The document points out that Mozambique recorded 611 road accidents in 2025, 76 fewer than the 687 registered in 2024, extending the downward trend observed over recent years. “Despite this trend, road fatalities have worsened. The number of people killed increased from 825 in 2024 to 830 in 2025, marking the second consecutive annual increase and the highest figure since 2021, when 1,101 people died on Mozambique’s roads”, reads the document. In 2022, road accidents claimed 808 lives.

items.title: Mozambique: Prices up 0.48% in October
items.summary: Prices in Mozambique increased by 0.48% in October, while year-on-year inflation remained broadly stable at 6.32%, below the Government’s forecast for 2026, according to data released on Monday by the National Statistics Institute (INE) According to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for October, the country recorded an acceleration in monthly inflation following the 0.16% increase observed in September, which had interrupted two consecutive months of deflation he divisions of Food and non-alcoholic beverages, Restaurants, hotels, cafés and similar establishments, and Transport made the largest contributions to the rise in prices, with positive impacts of approximately 0.29, 0.08 and 0.05 percentage points, respectively Among the products that contributed most to the increase in prices in October were fresh fish, which rose by 2.8%, onions (5.7%), second-hand light motor vehicles (5.4%), lettuce (9.8%), tomatoes (1.6%), horse mackerel (1.4%) and full meals in restaurants (0.9%).

items.title: Turkey pushes for transition at COP31 as coal burns
items.summary: The host of this year's UN climate summit remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels as it tries to inspire a global switch to clean energy As Turkey welcomes delegates to the 2026 UN climate talks in Antalya and pushes for cuts in global greenhouse gas emissions, it can point to surging renewable energy capacity at home The COP31 host has approved more than 33 gigawatts (GW) of battery storage projects since 2022 that can power over 27 million homes Among the largest battery project pipelines in Europe, this storage will complement fast-expanding wind and solar energy that today provides 22% of electricity in Turkey, up from 4.5% a decade ago Yet this clean energy upswing is a long way from compensating for the country's overreliance on fossil fuels Turkey's coal-fired electricity generation increased by roughly one-third in the last decade, and in 2024 overtook Germany and Poland, which previously had the highest coal power capacity in Europe before it began to decline To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video…

items.title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election
items.summary: Voters cast their ballots at a polling station during South Africa's local government elections in Johannesburg South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic" While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 31% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 65% 20 years ago The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second in the overall vote with 25%, retaining majority control of the city of Cape Town.

items.title: South Africa elections: ANC marks its worst-ever performance
items.summary: The African National Congress, the party of late liberation icon Nelson Mandela, slumped to its worst-ever result in South Africa's municipal election. Voters blame the ANC for water and electricity shortages South Africa's African National Congress (ANC) turned in a historically poor election performance , with the the final tally published on Sunday giving them less than 31% of the vote in Wednesday's municipal polls Their closes rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), won just under 25% of the vote The ANC also lost its majority in six of the eight metropolitan regions, South Africa 's Electoral Commission said Saturday. With no outright winner declared in several major cities, politicians are expected enter tough coalition talks to form municipal governments While the ANC remains the most popular party in the country, they have been struggling with growing backlash from voters. Many South Africans are frustrated by water and electricity shortages, with the ANC taking the blame for the poor state of municipalities.
